statement: We safely resolved 12,000 duplicate customer records using deterministic matching and manual review of candidates exceeding 0.6 confidence.
question: How many duplicate customer records can we merge with acceptable error rates?
decision: If merge precision > 98 percent and review queue catches 99 percent of false-positive candidates, we can safely deploy this to production.
grain: One organization's complete customer database as of 2026-09-01; merge was deterministic (exact match on email + phone) plus ML candidates at threshold 0.6, with all above-0.6 candidates manually reviewed by stewards.
_note: This example demonstrates master data gates M1-M6 for entity resolution and merge claims. It illustrates: threshold band partitioning (M1), survivorship rules (M2), false-merge cost asymmetry (M3), review sample evidence (M4/M5), and twin metrics match_rate + sampled_accuracy (M6).

uncertainty.method: Wilson score interval at 95 percent confidence, using observed accuracy from 200 human-labeled sampled pairs

not_established: Drift in match quality over time: the ML model was trained on 2024 customer data; data distributions may have changed since then.
Merge reversibility: the claim states a merge is irreversible in the current system (no time-travel to customer ID history), so a false merge must be caught before commit.
Seasonal effects: the sample was drawn from Q3 2026; Q1 seasonal customer records may have different match properties.
Cross-organization entity alignment: this is a single organization's internal deduplication, not a B2B entity resolution across vendors.
